meta.summary: Hides app prompts, link cards, media, views, reactions, avatars, subscriber counts; blur or grayscale media
meta.notes:
**Checked** 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-13, headless Chromium with an iPhone UA at 390x844, logged out, on `t.me/telegram`, `t.me/s/telegram`, `t.me/s/durov`, `t.me/s/contest`.

## Live counts (LIVE, querySelectorAll, `t.me/s/telegram` unless noted)

- `.tgme_channel_join_telegram` 1, `a.tgme_widget_message_link_preview` 4, `a.tgme_widget_message_photo_wrap` 3, `a.tgme_widget_message_video_player` 13, `.tgme_widget_message_views` 20. Landing `t.me/telegram`: `.tgme_head_right_btn` 1, `.tgme_page_additional` 1, `.tgme_page_extra` 1.
- New, `t.me/s/durov`: `.tgme_widget_message_user_photo` 20 visible, `.tgme_widget_message_reactions` 20, `.tgme_widget_message_reply` 1, `.tgme_widget_message_forwarded_from` 1, `.tgme_header_counter` 1, `.tgme_widget_message_author` 21, `.link_preview_image` 3, `.tgme_page_photo_image` 2 (1 visible: the header picture).
- `t.me/s/contest`: `.tgme_widget_message_reply` 3. `t.me/s/telegram` itself has no reactions, replies or forwards.

## Not worth a rule

`.tgme_channel_info` (the info card with counters) and `.tgme_footer` exist but are `display: none` at 390px, so hiding them does nothing on a phone. Polls, stickers, voice notes, documents and inline keyboards did not appear on any of the 10 public channels sampled, so no rule targets them.

## Web A rules (SOURCE, NOT verified live)

`web.telegram.org/a/` shows only the login QR logged out. `.WebPage`, `.MessageMeta .message-views` and `.Avatar` are plain, non-hashed class names in the open-source client (github.com/Ajaxy/telegram-tt: WebPage.tsx, MessageMeta.tsx, Avatar.scss). Reaction chips and chat-list badges use hashed CSS-module names there, so no Web A reaction rule exists. Fixture `web-a.html` is hand-written.

## Left alone on purpose

The View in Telegram button, Preview channel link, search box and post text. Hiding `.Avatar` is not offered (it would collapse chat rows), so Hide only affects t.me pages and Blur covers Web A too.
